title: Buzz documentation corpus node
description: Frontmatter contract for a canonical corpus node (ADR-0028: Markdown with YAML frontmatter). Validates the machine-checkable fields; the Markdown body carries the human-readable prose ADR-0029 governs.

id.description: Stable identifier for this node. Kebab-case. Never renamed once assigned, per ADR-0028's canonical-representation requirement that generated projections derive reproducibly from one source.

type.description: The corpus surface this node documents. Values are PRD #602's own enumerated list of in-scope surfaces, reused here rather than a second, independently invented taxonomy.

status.description: flagged is ADR-0029's 'unestablished/flagged' state: two same-claim-type authoritative sources contradict each other and a human has not yet resolved it. A flagged node is not simply low-confidence -- it names an unresolved conflict.

origin.description: Reuses ADR-0003's per-claim origin prefixes so origin stays a consistent vocabulary across the handbook and the corpus, rather than each corpus inventing its own.

audiences.description: Who this node is written for. Closed enum, not free text -- see COMPATIBILITY.md before adding a value.

evidence.description: The node's provenance ledger. One entry per claim, classified per launchpad/project-intelligence/CONTRACT.md's FACT/INFERENCE/TEAM_KNOWLEDGE contract (reused here, not reinvented).

relationships.description: Typed edges to other corpus nodes. Optional -- a node may have none. relationships.schema.json is the canonical source for this enum plus each type's directionality/inverse metadata; the $defs.relationship below is inlined rather than cross-file-$ref'd so this schema validates with a plain jsonschema.validate() call and no custom resolver. tests/test_schema.py asserts the two enum lists never drift apart.

target.description: The stable id (this schema's own `id` field) of the related node.

statement.description: The claim being made, one sentence.

evidence.description: Citations (paths, commit-pinned links, or similar). Required for FACT and INFERENCE -- see launchpad/project-intelligence/memory.py's enforced rule, not just CONTRACT.md's summary table.

confidence.description: Required (in addition to evidence) for INFERENCE only; forbidden on FACT and TEAM_KNOWLEDGE -- memory.py's __post_init__ raises if confidence is set on any other class.

provided_by.description: Who told the corpus this. Required for TEAM_KNOWLEDGE only; forbidden on FACT and INFERENCE -- memory.py's __post_init__ raises if provided_by is set on any other class. TEAM_KNOWLEDGE needs no evidence (it may optionally carry some) -- it is the class that exists for uncorroborated statements.
